category_title: At-risk students balancing full-time employment and parental responsibilities
minimal_context: The student is logging into the Novanet online instructional program to complete a self-paced lesson during their short school schedule.
dialogue:
TUTOR: Please log into the Novanet online instructional program and continue your self-paced lesson.

STUDENT: I only have my short 4-hour school schedule today. Do I really have to spend it on Novanet?

TUTOR: Yes, please go ahead and start the module.

STUDENT: I'm clicking through it, but I do not seem to learn from the online lessons.

TUTOR: Just keep reading through the screens and try your best.

STUDENT: I strongly feel that the program is boring. I'm expressing my discontent because I'm not learning anything, and I'm already frustrated by the delay in my class schedule changes.

options.A: Use quiet time as a supportive strategy to prevent emotional overload, having the student withdraw from the online program for a time-limited period.
options.B: Make explicit reference to workplace expectations, telling the student that a boss would not care about their frustration with the program or schedule.
options.C: Utilize differentiated instruction, such as guided practice, direct teaching, one-on-one instruction, technology, role play, games, group learning, peer tutoring, and a whatever-works approach.
options.D: Instruct the student that if they feel themselves getting angry about the online program, they should walk out and get a drink of water.
